## 16dfbdc731e1

**Classification: reproduced teaching shortcut and reproduced override-contract defects.** No source was changed.

Candidate rival: **fill every column between any two nonzero endpoints using the top endpoint’s color, without requiring endpoint colors to match**. It fits all three canonical pairs and all 1,200 ordinary generated grids sampled across bands because generated endpoint pairs always match.

The exact disagreement is `checks/audit/16dfbdc731e1/mismatched_input.json`. Two columns have matching endpoints and one has top/bottom colors 4 and 7. The intended rule fills only the matching columns; the rival also fills the mismatched gap with 4. The generator’s `self_check` rejects this input with `column 6 endpoint colors differ`, which confirms that the missing negative is outside current generated support. `mismatched_racket_output.json` and `authority_check.json` bind generator SHA-256 `ac8badb8a61133d893514d168dd1184ad2d2d43bc0ad18c5eaa811ec3bd0202d` and rule hash `4e66e5a34649`; Racket matches the independent intended output and disagrees with the rival.

The same source also reproduces exact-control defects: declared `grid_h=4`, `grid_h=18`, and `pairs=1` raise against narrower hardcoded ranges; unknown `bogus_axis` is accepted; a nominal 18×18 request returns 8×8; and `palette_kind`/`n_distinct_colors` can have no pixel effect. See `checks/audit/16dfbdc731e1/audit_probe.json` and `probe_shortcuts_and_overrides.py`.

A repair should include mismatched endpoint colors as an authored negative while keeping them out of the fill, reject unknown overrides, align declared domains with actual draws, and remove or make every advertised axis observable.
